I basically just posted the same thing in another, older thread, but I've just started smoking again and I'm interested in a vaporizer. I watched the Vape Critic's review of the Arizer Air, and I think I'd want a more portable vape with less maintenance required. Do you know of a vape like that?

The Pax and Pax2 are supposed to be pretty good although I don't know if it's as good as the Air; but it's very nice looking, smaller and a bit more expensive. If you want to drop some real coin though, the Crafty, by Storz and Bickel (the same people who make the Volcano) is supposed to be great. Both of these are supposed quite good options, though they are significantly more expensive than the Air and the Solo. Solo's are the predecessor to the air, and can be found quite cheap, but they're less portable.

For the money, the Air (and probably the Solo) from Arizer are both very good. Yes, you can't just pull them out of your pocket and go, but the stems come with caps, so you can pre-load a couple of bowls and vape quite easily. Logistically speaking, if you want the option of more than one session, the Air's preloaded stems actually make reloading easier. With smaller vaporizers, you'll have to grind up some bud and reload by hand while you're out and about. With the Air/Solo, you just pop out one stem, and pop in another. There are also a variety of after market stems and bubblers for the Air (and Solo) that can really make it quite versatile. I always have mine stashed on me with a couple of bowls, just in case the mood strikes me. When it was my only vaporizer, I was very happy with it.
Pax is better than the Air. Vapes more evenly & (in my experience) better battery life.

The battery on mine started to hold less and less, the airflow got tighter since there isn't a straight through hole from the bottom of the mouth piece pipe to the actual mouth piece for easy cleaning.

Just the design was really cool and if you could somehow clean the airflow in the mouthpiece (since there is like an "L" shape near the top where pipe cleaners would jam against), keep the spring clean, and always have plenty of lube I could recommend it as a really stealth unit.
